CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay inside the G20 90-day window and treat the just-concluded Beijing working talks as the opening of a purchase-first negotiation, not a settlement. Offer additional agricultural, energy, and market-access buys that Washington can score as progress, while refusing irreversible industrial-policy or Made-in-China-2025 dismantlement and keeping Meng/Huawei on a separate legal track. Do not add tariffs, expand detentions, or otherwise give hawks in Washington a pretext to restore the January List-3 hike to 25 percent.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. Combined Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B of Chinese exports (25% on $50B plus 10% on ~$200B as of 24 Sep 2018), and the 1 Jan 2019 lift of List 3 to 25% was only suspended, not cancelled, with a hard date around 2 Mar if talks fail. Firm-level targeting is real: the 16 Apr 2018 ZTE denial order showed a US component cutoff can shut a national champion, and the 1 Dec 2018 arrest of Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou on a US extradition request — the same day as the Buenos Aires truce — puts China's flagship telecom firm and a politically sensitive family in the dispute. The real economy is already softening: official Q3 2018 GDP was 6.5% (slowest since 2009), factories in Dongguan were cutting hours and sending migrant workers home unpaid, auto sales had plunged, and industrial production growth eased to 5.7% YoY in Dec 2018. That maps near the CHN +0.5 anchor (export sectors hit, Huawei targeting, unemployment risk in export hubs) but is pulled down from +0.5 because FX pressure has eased (CNY from ~6.97 in late Oct to 6.81 on 9 Jan), reserves recovered to ~$3.11T, merchandise exports rebounded in the latest reading, and the March cliff has not yet fired. Action should be negotiate, not escalate or concede. China has already used most of its tariff ammunition (matching $50B plus 5–10% on ~$60B) and further escalation would likely trigger the 25% List-3 hike that Trump has explicitly tied to a failed 90-day window. Mid-level talks that ran 7–9 Jan were extended a third day with reported progress on farm/energy purchases and GM-crop approvals, while remaining far apart on structural IP, forced-transfer, and enforcement — exactly the split China Daily flagged by rejecting "unreasonable concessions." Purchase offers keep the truce alive and exploit US farm-belt politics without locking in structural reform; full rollback or concede_purchases is premature because Washington has not tabled a matching tariff stand-down and Lighthizer is treating 1 Mar as a hard deadline. Hold would waste the only live channel before that deadline.
key_factors: US Section 301 still covers ~$250B of Chinese goods; List-3 10%→25% hike only paused until ~2 Mar 2019
Huawei/Meng arrest plus the ZTE denial-order precedent is firm-level tech targeting, not just tariffs
Domestic slowdown (Q3 GDP 6.5%, factory hour cuts, auto slump) raises the cost of a failed truce
Yuan and reserves have stabilized since the G20; threat is high but not a financial-stability crisis
Beijing talks (7–9 Jan) advanced purchases and market access, not structural IP/industrial-policy demands
China has little unused tariff space; further escalation would likely restore the 25% List-3 rate

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires dinner: Trump and Xi agree to a 90-day negotiation window. Planned Jan 1, 2019 hike of List 3 from 10% to 25% is suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
Trade talks resume in Beijing (working / mid-level). China discusses increased purchases of US goods; structural issues remain open.
China industrial production YoY index latest 105.7 (Dec 2018), down 0.4 points over the window — growth still positive but easing.
CNY/USD weakened toward 6.97 in late Oct then recovered to 6.8117 on 2019-01-09 after the G20 truce.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.107T in Jan 2019 after an Oct trough — pressure, not a reserve crisis.
Talks extended a third day; progress reported on farm/energy purchases and market access, sides further apart on structural reforms and enforcement. China Daily: no unreasonable concessions.
Q3 growth 6.5% slowest since 2009; auto sales plunged; Dongguan factories cutting hours and sending workers home on unpaid leave; pressure on Xi for a deal.
Beijing separated the Meng arrest from trade talks because an increase in tariffs threatens China while the economy is vulnerable.
